scope: HOSTED ARRIVAL round (PLAN_V4 task 3). Not the bundle on disk: the six hosted endpoints a claude.ai user would connect by URL, reached the way that user reaches them - GET https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/connect to mint a fresh anonymous token, then `claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url>` with NO headers. Eight scenarios in one conversation (plus one new session for the last), covering onboarding, hours and receipts, a cross-currency invoice with its document, a Word proposal, a two-zone meeting, the free cap and its checkout link, the tier question, and server-side persistence.
method: Six local-scope MCP entries in a temp project /private/tmp/uv52: invoice, time-tracker, expense-tracker, timezone, docx, currency, each as https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/<server>/t/anon_49285ffeb6a7468bb57086eaf8df1e80, no --header anywhere. `claude mcp list`: all six Connected. Per-tool allowlist of 103 entries written from a live tools/list POSTed to each endpoint (12+14+14+11+14+10 = 75 tools, plus underscore variants of the two hyphenated server names as insurance). Client: claude -p --model sonnet --output-format stream-json --verbose --max-turns 18, one --session-id then seven --resume, and one brand-new --session-id for scenario 8. Free tier throughout (fresh anonymous token, tier free, bound false). No fixture, no seed: every row was created by the model in this run. Clock: run start 16:24 UTC Thursday 2026-09-03. Tool-call counts exclude the client's own ToolSearch schema lookups.
rubric: 3 = correct, right numbers, no clarification. 2 = correct but needed a second turn, a workaround, or left the user a gap to close. 1 = partially wrong, or asked for something the tool could infer. 0 = failed.

arrival.connect_page: GET https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/connect -> 200 text/html, 7097 bytes, minted anon_49285ffeb6a7468bb57086eaf8df1e80 and printed a ready URL for all twelve endpoints (eleven servers plus whoami)
arrival.registration: six `claude mcp add --transport http --scope local <name> <url>` calls, no headers; `claude mcp list` reported all six Connected on the first try, before and after the mid-round redeploy

scenarios.prompt: I am Lucky Strike Software in Warsaw, VAT PL1234567890, EUR, 23% VAT, 14-day terms.
scenarios.note: One hosted call, every fact landed, and the response named the shared profile at mcp-servers/profile/business.json and the seven servers that read it. Two deductions, both visible in out/s1.jsonl: the model then wrote the same facts into the CLI's own project memory directory (D-R31 class, client side, on top of a tool response that had just said 'You do not need to repeat it anywhere else'), and no timezone reached the profile - 'in Warsaw' was used for the address only, and business_set neither inferred Europe/Warsaw nor asked, so nothing declared the home zone R9's D-R35 fix reads.

scenarios.prompt: Log 4 hours today on Nova at 90 EUR and a 61.50 EUR Adobe receipt for Nova.
scenarios.note: entry 3ebc2fda: Nova, 2026-09-03 09:00, 4.00 h, EUR 90.00/h, EUR 360.00, billable. expense 13e6893d: EUR 61.50 gross = net EUR 50.00 + VAT EUR 11.50 at 23%, the rate taken from the shared profile written one sentence earlier and named as its source. Both verified by a curl tools/call against the hosted endpoints afterwards.

scenarios.prompt: Invoice Nova for that in USD at today's ECB rate and give me the document.
scenarios.note: The chain is right and unusually complete: today's ECB rate (1 EUR = 1.1615 USD, dated 2026-09-03), the receipt pulled through expense_to_invoice as a net line in USD, INV-2026-0001 created, the document rendered, and both the time entry and the expense marked billed against the invoice number so nothing can be billed twice. The document is real: GET of the download link returns 200 text/html, 1906 bytes, carrying Lucky Strike Software, PL1234567890 and USD 585.78 - the same total as the prose. Deduction: the hours line was passed as unit_price 104.535 and the server rounded it to 104.54 before multiplying by 4, so the line is USD 418.16 where 4 x 90 x 1.1615 = 418.14, and the invoice total is USD 585.78 against 585.75 for the stated rate. Three cents, silently, with no note that a fractional unit price was rounded (D-R46). Second, smaller gap: the tool is called invoice_pdf and returns HTML to print - the model disclosed it, but 'give me the document' is answered one step short.

scenarios.prompt: Write a two-paragraph proposal for Nova's phase 2, 6,000 EUR, as a Word file.
scenarios.note: One call, PROP-2026-0001, and the file is a real .docx: PK\x03\x04 header, content-type application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, content-disposition filename nova-phase-2.docx, 10985 bytes. word/document.xml carries the letterhead from the shared profile (Lucky Strike Software, Warsaw, Poland, VAT PL1234567890), '[add: email]' rather than an invented address, zero @ characters, EUR 6,000.00, and the two summary paragraphs as two real w:p runs with no literal backslash-n. Deduction: proposal_create requires scope, deliverables and a timeline, so a request for a two-paragraph proposal came back as a multi-section document with a 4-phase timeline the model invented. It disclosed the invention and offered to correct it, which is why this is 2 and not 1 (D-R47).

scenarios.prompt: Find a one-hour slot next week with Tom in Austin inside 9 to 17 for both of us.
scenarios.note: It checked for a saved contact first, then searched Mon 2026-09-07 to Fri 09-11 with both work windows at 09:00-17:00, resolving the bare place name 'Austin' server-side. Five slots, all the same hour, fairness 3.50 h each: 16:00-17:00 Europe/Warsaw = 09:00-10:00 America/Chicago, which is the only hour two 9-to-17 days share across a 7-hour offset (CEST +02, CDT -05). The model said exactly that - the choice is which day, not which hour - and offered to save Tom and to emit an .ics.

scenarios.prompt: Add three more clients with invoices so I hit the free limit.
scenarios.note: Turn one refused to act and asked two questions, because license_status showed tier free and an upgrade URL and nothing else: no cap, no usage, no pointer to where the caps are written, so the model could not tell whether an invoice cap existed and said so. Turn two ran it: INV-2026-0002 and INV-2026-0003 created, and the third was refused with 'You have already created 3 invoices in 2026-09. The free tier allows 3 invoices per calendar month' plus the upgrade line. The checkout path then verified end to end: the link carries ?tenant=anon_49285ffeb6a7468bb57086eaf8df1e80, GET with x-mcp-probe:1 returns 303 to checkout.stripe.com, and `stripe checkout sessions list --live --limit 1` shows that session with metadata {probe:1, product:invoice, tenant:anon_49285ffeb6a7468bb57086eaf8df1e80} and client_reference_id equal to the token. The one-turn miss is D-R44, fixed in remote/ this round.

scenarios.prompt: What is my tier and how do I upgrade?
tools: license_status x5 (docx, expense-tracker, time-tracker, timezone, currency)
scenarios.note: Answered correctly in one turn - free on all six, one anonymous token, per-server $19 with a tenant-carrying link each, $39 for every server - and it refused to complete a purchase itself. Two deductions. whoami is an HTTP GET, not a tool on any endpoint, so there is no one call that answers 'what is my tier': the model paid one license_status per connected server, five in a row, and stitched the answer together. And the $39 every-server price was named with no link, because license_status and the cap text both mentioned the bundle price without ever mentioning /buy/bundle, which exists and 303s to Stripe with the same tenant metadata. Both are hosted-side and both are fixed in remote/ this round (D-R43, D-R50 partially).

scenarios.prompt: What did I invoice this month? (brand-new session, same six URLs, no conversation history)
scenarios.note: One invoice_list {from: 2026-09-01, to: 2026-09-30} against the same URL, from a session that had never seen any of the earlier turns, returned all three invoices created above with the right numbers, clients, currencies and due dates. The model totalled the two EUR invoices to EUR 2,460.00 and deliberately kept the USD 585.78 separate rather than mixing currencies, and it flagged that two of the three are placeholder clients. Server-side persistence per anonymous token, at the same URL, with nothing pasted.

totals.note: Not comparable to r9's 23/24: r9 re-scored eight known-weak sentences against the bundle on disk, r10 scores eight fresh scenarios against six hosted endpoints reached by URL with no headers. The three 3s are the ones where the hosted path adds nothing to break; four of the five deductions are about what the endpoint tells the model about itself, not about what it computes.

verification.post_fix: license_status now reports source 'URL path segment (/mcp/<server>/t/<token>)' on the path form, 'URL query parameter (?token=)' on ?token=, 'Authorization: Bearer' on the header form, all three confirmed live; bundleUrl, price_usd, limits and guide present; the cap text now carries the /buy/bundle link; whoami reports token_arrived_via. node scripts/validate.mjs: remote 31/31, run 50 252/252

defects.title: license_status told every caller its token came from an Authorization header, including the URL-token callers who have no header field
defects.repro: POST https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/invoice/t/<token> tools/call license_status -> "source": "Authorization: Bearer", on a request with no Authorization header at all. Same for ?token=.
defects.fix: remote/src/shims/ctx.ts gains RequestCtx.authVia; remote/src/index.ts records which of the three forms actually carried the token in Auth.via (header wins when both are present, as before) and threads it into the request context; remote/src/shims/license.ts reports it as `source`. GET /mcp/whoami also reports token_arrived_via. Re-vendored and deployed (version 7d3f5812).

defects.title: the $39 every-server price was quoted in every free-cap message and never linked, although /buy/bundle exists and carries the tenant
defects.repro: any free-cap refusal, e.g. the 4th invoice_create: 'Pro is a one-time $19 (or $39 for every server, lifetime). Buy at https://mcp.zovo.one/buy/invoice?tenant=...' - the $39 has no URL, and scenario 7 relayed the price to the user with no way to act on it, while GET /buy/bundle?tenant=<token> with x-mcp-probe:1 already 303s to Stripe with metadata.tenant set.
defects.fix: remote/src/shims/license.ts: new bundleUrl() building /buy/bundle?tenant=<anonToken>, inlined in upgradeText next to the $39 and returned from license_status as bundleUrl, with price_usd {single, every_server}.

defects.title: license_status carried no free-tier limit information, so a model asked about 'the free limit' had to discover the caps by tripping them
defects.repro: /private/tmp/uv52/out/s6.jsonl. Prompt 'Add three more clients with invoices so I hit the free limit.' -> one license_status, which returns only product, tier, transport, tenant, source, upgradeUrl. The model answered 'I do not see a numeric cap on invoice creation itself' and asked two clarifying questions instead of acting. The cap is real and fires on the 4th invoice of the month.
defects.fix: remote/src/shims/license.ts: license_status now also returns `limits` (stating plainly that this tool does not count usage, that a call over a cap is refused with the cap named, and where the per-server caps are written) and `guide` (https://mcp.zovo.one/guides/mcp-server-free-vs-pro). Usage counters are per-server state in servers/*, out of scope for a remote-only fix.

defects.title: license_activate told a URL-token caller to reconnect with a header, which is exactly the field their client does not have
defects.repro: tools/list on any hosted endpoint: license_activate's description and response name only 'Authorization: Bearer MCPL1....'. A claude.ai or Claude Desktop custom connector cannot set one - which is why the URL forms exist.
defects.fix: remote/src/shims/license.ts: the description and the response now lead with https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/<product>/t/MCPL1...., keep the header as the alternative, and add that a purchase made from a ?tenant=<token> link needs nothing pasted at all because Pro is already on for the same connection and the same data.

defects.title: invoice_create rounds a fractional unit_price to minor units and then multiplies, so a converted hourly line drifts from the rate it names
defects.repro: hosted or local: invoice_create {currency: USD, items: [{description: '... at 1.1615', quantity: 4, unit_price: 104.535, tax_rate: 23}]} -> unit_price_minor 10454, gross_minor 41816. 4 x 90 x 1.1615 = 418.14, and INV-2026-0001's total_minor 58578 is 3 cents above the ECB conversion the invoice cites. Nothing in the response says a unit price was rounded.
defects.fix_direction: either accept and keep sub-minor unit prices for the line total (round once, at the line), or say so: the response already explains 'each line was rounded first and then summed' for the total, and should name the unit price it changed and by how much. Both paths are in servers/invoice, which this round was not allowed to edit.

defects.title: proposal_create's required sections turn 'a two-paragraph proposal' into three sections of invented content
defects.repro: /private/tmp/uv52/out/s4.jsonl. The prompt asks for two paragraphs and EUR 6,000; the schema requires scope, deliverables and a timeline, so the model wrote a 4-phase timeline and a deliverables list nobody asked for, then told the user it had. word/document.xml carries all of it.
defects.fix_direction: make scope/deliverables/timeline optional, or have the tool emit a placeholder line the way the letterhead already emits '[add: email]' instead of letting the model fill the gap.

defects.title: 'I am ... in Warsaw' set an address but no timezone, and business_set neither infers one nor asks
defects.repro: /private/tmp/uv52/out/s1.jsonl: invoice_business_set {name, address: 'Warsaw, Poland', vat_id, default_currency, default_tax_rate, payment_terms_days} -> profile written with no timezone field, and the response does not mention the gap. R9's D-R35 fix (stamping 'yesterday' in the declared home zone) reads exactly that field.
defects.fix_direction: when address names a place and timezone is absent, either resolve it (timezone already resolves bare place names - scenario 5 passed zone 'Austin') or say in the response which downstream behaviour is running on the machine zone until it is set.

defects.title: the model copied the business facts into the CLI's project memory directory immediately after the tool said not to repeat them anywhere
defects.repro: /private/tmp/uv52/out/s1.jsonl: after invoice_business_set returned '...which docx, expense-tracker, recurring, time-tracker, timezone, resume and clauses all read. You do not need to repeat it anywhere else.', the model called Write on .../projects/-private-tmp-uv52/memory/business_profile.md and then rewrote MEMORY.md. Two copies of one identity, free to drift.
defects.fix_direction: client behaviour, not fixable server-side; the r9 wording is already as explicit as it can be. Worth re-checking whenever the memory tool is in the harness.

defects.title: whoami is reachable only as an HTTP GET, so 'what is my tier' costs one license_status per connected server
defects.repro: scenario 7: five license_status calls in a row (docx, expense-tracker, time-tracker, timezone, currency) plus the invoice one from scenario 6, because no tool spans the connection and GET /mcp/whoami/t/<token> is not callable from an MCP client. The GET itself works and is richer than license_status (tenant, tier, bound, kind, rate_limit_per_hour, how, connect, guide, and now token_arrived_via).
defects.fix_direction: the per-endpoint half is closed: license_status now carries the bundle link, the prices, the limits pointer and the real auth form, so one call answers the tier question completely. A cross-endpoint answer would need whoami registered as a tool on every endpoint, which is a vendored-server change rather than a remote-only one.
